Add a new utility (a game, dice roller, spinner, scoreboard, timer, etc.) to
the Games library at `/games`. This skill captures the pattern the library
was built on so every utility looks, behaves, and is edited the same way.

## Hard rule: generate assets yourself

**Every image or icon a new utility needs must be generated by you, not
requested from or provided by the user.** Never ask the user for a logo,
card image, or icon file, and never leave a placeholder expecting them to
supply one. Draw it yourself as inline/hand-authored SVG (see "Creating
assets" below) and commit it as a real file in `src/assets/games/`. The
per-utility drawer already lets the user replace it with their own upload
later if they want — that UI is the intended way a user ever swaps an
asset, not a prompt from you asking them for one up front.

## How the library works

- `src/features/games/utilities.ts` is the single registry of built-in
  utilities (`GAME_UTILITIES`). Each entry is `{ key, path, defaultName,
  defaultDescription, defaultImage }`.
- `src/pages/Games.tsx` renders `GAME_UTILITIES` (merged with any per-user
  overrides) as a 2-column grid of `GameUtilityCard`s.
- Tapping a card navigates to its `path`. Long-pressing a card (via
  `useLongPress`, see `src/lib/useLongPress.ts`) opens
  `EditGameUtilityDrawer`, letting the user override the name, description,
  and image for that one utility. Overrides live in the `game_utilities`
  Supabase table (per-user, keyed by `utility_key`) and images upload to the
  `game-images` storage bucket — both already exist; you don't need to
  create them again for a new utility, just add a row's worth of code.
- Each utility is its own route+page under `src/pages/`, added to
  `src/App.tsx`'s lazy-loaded route list, e.g. `games/dice` →
  `src/pages/DiceRoller.tsx`.

## Steps to add a new utility

1. **Design the interaction first.** Decide what state it needs (dice
   values, card deck, timer, score), and whether it needs persistence
   (localStorage for local prefs like die count; Supabase only if it needs
   to sync/be shared).
2. **Create the asset(s)** for the card image (and any in-utility art) —
   see "Creating assets" below. Save under `src/assets/games/<name>.svg`.
3. **Register the utility** in `src/features/games/utilities.ts`:
   - Add the new key to `GameUtilityKey`.
   - Add an entry to `GAME_UTILITIES` with `key`, `path` (e.g.
     `/games/<slug>`), `defaultName`, `defaultDescription`, and
     `defaultImage` (import the SVG asset).
4. **Build the utility's own page** under `src/pages/<Utility>.tsx`,
   following the existing pattern in `src/pages/DiceRoller.tsx`:
   - Back button (`ChevronLeft` + `Link to="/games"`) and a title in the
     header. Read the *current* display name via `fetchGameUtilities()` so
     a user-renamed card is reflected as the page title, falling back to
     `defaultName`.
   - Any core game logic (e.g. randomness) lives in small, pure,
     testable helper functions — don't inline `Math.random()` calls
     scattered through JSX; prefer `crypto.getRandomValues` for anything
     resembling dice/cards/shuffling so it's not trivially predictable.
   - Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for any animation (see the
     `reducedMotion` check in `DiceRoller.tsx`) — shorten or skip motion,
     never make it required to understand the result.
   - Use `haptic(...)` from `src/lib/haptics.ts` at natural interaction
     points (selection, action, success) the way other utilities do.
   - Persist small per-device preferences (like a selected mode/count) in
     `localStorage`, wrapped in try/catch (private browsing can throw).
5. **Wire the route** in `src/App.tsx`: add a `lazy(() =>
   import('./pages/<Utility>'))` and a `<Route path="games/<slug>"
   element={<Utility />} />` next to the existing `games/dice` route.
6. **Reuse existing UI primitives** — `Button`, `Drawer`/`DrawerContent`,
   `cn()` from `src/utils.ts` — rather than inventing new styling patterns.
   Match the visual language already established by `Games.tsx` /
   `GameUtilityCard.tsx` / `DiceRoller.tsx` (rounded-2xl cards, `bg-card`,
   `text-muted-foreground` secondary text, etc).
7. **Verify visually** before considering it done — follow the root
   `CLAUDE.md`'s "Testing the UI in this sandbox" section (stub Supabase
   env vars, temporarily swap `main.tsx`, drive with Playwright) to
   screenshot the new card in the grid and the utility itself mid- and
   post-interaction. Revert the `main.tsx` swap and delete `.env.local`
   afterward — never commit either.

## Creating assets

No image or icon should ever come from the user for a game utility — you
generate all of it, every time. Two things need art:

**a) The library card image** (`defaultImage`, ~4:3, shown at card size in
a 2-column grid — keep it simple/bold, it renders small):
- Build it as raw SVG (see `src/assets/games/dice-card.svg` for the
  reference example: gradients via `<linearGradient>`/`<radialGradient>`,
  a soft background, one or two hero elements, a subtle drop shadow via a
  blurred ellipse, a couple of small dot/sparkle details for texture).
- Favor a `viewBox` around `400x300`, flat/gradient fills (no photographic
  effects, no external images/fonts, no raster embeds) so it stays crisp
  at small sizes and has zero network/asset dependencies.
- Save as `src/assets/games/<slug>-card.svg` and `import` it as a module
  (Vite resolves the `.svg` import to a URL string, same as
  `diceCardImage` in `utilities.ts`).

**b) In-utility art** (e.g. die faces, card faces, tokens): prefer small
React components that render inline `<svg>` with `viewBox="0 0 100 100"`
(see `src/features/games/DieFace.tsx`) rather than static image files,
whenever the art needs to vary by state (a die's pip count, a card's rank)
or be composed into CSS animation/3D transforms (see `Die3D.tsx`'s use of
`transform-style: preserve-3d` and per-face `rotateX/Y` placement). This
keeps the art crisp at any size, themeable via `currentColor` /
gradients if needed, and avoids shipping dozens of near-duplicate image
files for every state.

General asset rules:
- Never fetch, link to, or embed any external image/icon/font URL.
- Never leave a `TODO: add image` placeholder — always ship a finished
  asset in the same change.
- Keep SVGs hand-written and readable (named gradients, comments for
  non-obvious geometry) rather than pasting minified/tool-exported markup.
- Match the existing palette/rounding language (`rounded-2xl` cards,
  the teal/felt + off-white dice look) unless the new utility has a good
  reason to diverge — reuse gradient stop colors across utilities where it
  makes sense so the library feels like one family, not a grab-bag.

## Non-goals

- Don't add a new Supabase table/bucket per utility — the shared
  `game_utilities` table + `game-images` bucket already covers per-user
  name/description/image overrides for any utility. Only add new schema if
  the utility itself needs to persist gameplay state across sessions/devices
  (e.g. a running score log), and scope it to that utility's own table.
- Don't make long-press do anything other than open the edit drawer, and
  don't make tap do anything other than navigate — keep that contract
  consistent across every card in the grid.
